parsed.main_gap: Lemma 4’s crucial tree-component claim is asserted without proof, though it can be repaired by a short edge-count, bipartition, and triangle-inequality argument.

errors.description: The lower bound depends entirely on an omitted graph argument. One must show the graph has a tree component, bipartition it, and verify that its signed vertex-weight sum consists of paired-part differences plus possibly the lone unpaired part.
errors.quote: By a tree-component argument on the multigraph whose vertices are the original pieces $0,1,\dots,n$ and whose edges are the pairs $P_i$, there is a set $V_T\subseteq\{0,\dots,n\}$ and signs $s:V_T\to\{\pm1\}$ such that the signed sum $\Xi:=\sum_{j\in V_T}s(j)\,q_j$ satisfies $|\Xi|\le\sum_i\varepsilon_i+[M\text{ odd}]\,a_M$ (standard; details omitted).

parsed.notes: The answer, picking-phase reduction, signed-sum property, and upper-bound construction are otherwise coherent and correct. The sole omission is central but readily filled in a few rigorous sentences.
